verdict: OK to lend in Aurangabad auto components — pursue EV-capable tier-2 suppliers with tight covenants; avoid single-OEM, ICE-engine-dependent units.
title: Aurangabad auto & auto components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) runs on two anchors: the Bajaj Auto Waluj plant and the Skoda Auto Volkswagen India facility, both of which have had stop-start histories — the local coverage records a COVID-era shutdown, a 50% pay cut and a union shutdown appeal at Bajaj [1]. **A component supplier here is a press-and-machine shop that converts steel, aluminium and bought-out castings into brackets, shafts and sub-assemblies, and sells them to one or two OEMs on schedule.** Cash is made on the conversion margin, not the metal; the OEM sets the price and the payment clock.

## Where value and cash sit
**Pricing power is thin and the working-capital cycle is long.** ICRA's two-wheeler methodology flags high competitive intensity forcing high operating efficiency [8], and a rated component peer shows gross current assets averaging 160-170 days [10]. Capex is press and CNC capacity — lumpy, and debt-funded capex that pushes Debt/EBITDA past 2.5-2.75 times is a stated rating red flag [10].

## What has changed now
**Demand is strong but margins are being squeezed by input costs.** Motherson Sumi Wiring's Q2 profit rose 35% to Rs 223 crore on revenue up 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore [4]; Lumax beat Q2 2026 estimates and lifted its growth target [7]; but ASK Automotive reported record revenue with aluminium squeezing margins [5], and Elara expects Q4FY26 EBITDA growth of about 21% with commodity risk [6]. Locally, CSN is being described as a rising EV hub on the back of JSW investment [2] — that is a LinkedIn post, not audited data, so treat it as a lead, not a fact. The Bajaj plant news [1] is old (COVID-era) and should not drive today's decision.

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue tier-2 suppliers already shipping EV or powertrain-agnostic parts** — ASK's order wins span braking and aluminium lightweighting across EV [5], and CRISIL warns that engine-and-related-part suppliers face obsolescence risk as EVs spread [11]. Avoid single-OEM, diesel-injection-dependent units. Structure: receivables-backed CC as the core limit, LC for metal imports, and a term loan only against a confirmed OEM nomination letter. Take monthly: stock-and-receivable statements, OEM payment advices, and a quarterly Debt/EBITDA certificate.

- **Aluminium/steel input cost spike without a pass-through clause (monthly)** -> re-run the margin; if EBITDA falls below the level that services debt at 2.5x, restructure to LC-only. - **Order book shifting from ICE engine parts to EV parts (quarterly)** -> this is good; increase limit for EV-nominated suppliers, freeze for ICE-only. - **Debt/EBITDA above 2.5-2.75 times (quarterly)** -> stop fresh capex lending [10]. - **OEM plant shutdown or wage dispute at Waluj or SAVWIPL (event-based)** -> freeze new sanctions until production resumes [1].
